status: Research-only bounded alternative for captured ceiling-height/climate controls; no product edits

competitor: general room dimensions and temperature change

scope: Steady sensible heat loss through an entered envelope UA plus outdoor air exchange. Does not claim HVAC equipment sizing, Manual J compliance, total cooling load or competitor coefficient parity.

inputs.requirement: Positive finite dimensions; ceiling height affects volume. If building component areas are derived, exposed wall area also changes.
Entered overall heat-loss coefficient; or sum explicitly entered U-value times exposed component area. Do not infer from good/average/poor insulation.
Nonnegative actual operating air exchange assumption. Do not accept blower-door ACH50 as natural ACH without an independently supported conversion.
Nonnegative heating design difference, or computed from indoor and outdoor design temperatures. Climate category alone is insufficient.

equations.envelopeUA: sum(U_i * A_i), W/K, when components are supplied
equations.temperatureDifference: deltaTK = deltaTF * 5/9, without adding or subtracting 32

controlsGuidance: Keep the existing ENERGY STAR area guide independent. Its ceiling-height note is qualitative, not a license to scale area loads linearly with height.

Use a manually entered outdoor design temperature for climate until a versioned, suitable local design-temperature source is implemented. Do not assign undocumented coefficients to Boston, Houston or generic climate labels.
Effective envelope UA must include windows, thermal bridges and exposed boundary assumptions. Do not treat ground or conditioned-adjacent surfaces as outdoor exposure automatically.
Use one canonical SI volumetric coefficient for unit equivalence; the rounded imperial 0.018 coefficient will not be exactly equivalent to 1207 J/(m3 K).
Expose conduction and air exchange separately. The air estimate assumes constant volumetric heat capacity at a stated reference condition.
No latent, solar, occupant/appliance gains, wind/stack model, duct losses, equipment capacity/efficiency or transient warm-up. These are not covered by this bounded model.

primarySources.title: Hawaii State Energy Office building energy efficiency workshop
primarySources.support: Q=U*A*temperature difference*time; divide by time for steady heat flow.

primarySources.title: NREL building thermal envelope test report
primarySources.support: Dry air volumetric heat capacity 1.207 kJ/(m3 C) at sea level and 21.1 C; fixed ACH test condition.
primarySources.retrieval: Primary indexed PDF extract; direct PDF retrieval returned 502.

primarySources.title: DOE-hosted University of Minnesota building science course, 2016
primarySources.support: Air heat loss = 0.018 * ACH * volume * temperature difference in Btu/h with volume in cubic feet and difference in F. Rounded imperial coefficient.
primarySources.retrieval: Primary indexed slide text; direct request timed out.

primarySources.title: ENERGY STAR room air conditioners
primarySources.support: Area table assumes 8-foot ceiling; shade/sun adjustments and extra people/kitchen adjustments. No published numerical ceiling-height multiplier or Boston/Houston coefficient.

Regional design temperature or detailed material assembly presets require their own verified dataset; no invented presets.
